title: From Newtonian Mechanics to Quantum Electrodynamics: A Unified Framework on the Invariance and Transformation of Mass and Energy
content: This paper examines the conceptual boundary and governing principles connecting classical Newtonian mechanics, Einsteinian mass-energy equivalence, and Planckian quantum electrodynamics. In low-velocity macroscopic dynamics, mechanical energy transformations proceed under strict mass invariance, rendering relativistic corrections unnecessary. However, in complete radioactive decay or particle-antiparticle annihilation of a resting mass, intrinsic rest-frame energy converts directly into quantum electromagnetic energy. By linking rest-frame energy directly with Planck’s quantum formulation relating photon energy to radiation frequency and wavelength, the study demonstrates that the cumulative radiant energy strictly conserves the system's initial rest energy, establishing the fundamental equivalence between initial rest energy and total emitted photonic field energy. This paper details the structural transition from classical Newtonian mechanics to quantum field energy conservation without relying on intermediate relativistic momentum formulations.
